[b] June 6, 2028: Dicussions[/b]

Henri XVII sat across the table from the president of the state, the duchess Eleonore of Lorraine, a fresh pot of coffee bubbling before them as the clock on the wall ticked monotonously.

Have you heard of this unification movement? Asked Henri.

I have been informed, it doesnt seem to be anything concerning, replied Eleonore.

That is not a reassuring statement, you know something, replied Henri XVII.

Eleonore looked down and then to the side before sighing and replying, I have been in contact with a Monsieur Zedde, apparently he is a member of the International Association for the Reunification of Rosenmarkke and Montfleur, 

The king smirked, Of course you did,

What? Laughed Eleonore, He reached out to me, she scoffed.

Yes of course, anyways, do go on 

Yes, he has informed me they are writing a petition of grievances against the Rosenmarkket government, she continued.

The king raised an eyebrow, A petition? 

Yes, and he was wondering if you would consider looking at it, continued Eleonore.

Henri scoffed, Does he think I am an editor?

No, but he thinks you are a path to legitimacy, 

He is a madman then? Asked Henri.

Perhaps, joked Eleonore.

The king sniffed and then sipped his coffee, nearly spitting it out in surprise as an aid rushed in crying, Sir! Sir!

Henri turned, his face aghast at the disruption, What is it, spit it out boy,

I have been told to inform you that there is a group of men who demand to see you, the aid stated.

Henri looked at Eleonore who gave a confused look back at him, Who did they say they were? Asked Henri.

Members of some international association, they carried canes, we tried to take them away, but they threatened to smash the marble in the grand salon, replied the aid.

Oh heavens, come, let us go meet them, clapped Henri as he rose from the chair.

The aid, the king, and the president of the state made quick to the grand salon where they could hear the men chatting calmly, though the aid insisted on announcing the king, Henri was not in the mood for it.

Entering the room he saw the men, there were eight of them, all dressed in waistcoats and wigs, a few carrying canes, others carrying folders. As the king entered, the conversation stopped and they all bowed politely.

Henri gave a slight smile, clapped his hands and said, Gentlemen, to what do we owe the pleasure?

That one is Mr. Zedde, whispered Eleonore siding up to the king and pointing to a figure, the king nodded.

Your majesty, my name is Antoine LeMaine, I am the head of the Montfleurois caucus within our organization, said a man dressed in a pink waistcoat and wig, bowing in the old way.

Pleasure to meet you, replied the king, moving to shake the man's hand.

Gentlemen, please, sit, motioned the king to the couches in the room, I am already familiar with your cause, but I am intrigued to hear more,

Well your majesty, intoned the one called Zedde, First we wish to present you a gift, he motioned for one of the men to produce the gift which was a black walnut cane with a gold and diamond encrusted top, A cane from the city of Rosé, 

Henri gave a tight lipped smile as the can was handed to him, Ah, Rosé, the cane capital of East Elseyr, he said attempting to hide the sarcasm in his voice.

The gentlemen would politely clap, with those with canes tapping them lightly on the floor, nearly causing a servant who had been walking by to faint at the sight.

Now, lets get to business, what are you doing? What are your goals? Asked the king sitting down.

Well sir, Rosenmarkke has been in a bad spot recently, the government is practically gone, and well we are at risk of fracturing, replied Zedde.

That is clearly the case, replied the king.

So we seek to re-unite the country with its motherland, continued Zedde.

I see. Are you familiar with the Act of Settlement of 1887? Asked the king.

Yes, replied Zedde.

We recognized your independence then, did we not? Continued the king pressing on.

Yes, replied Zedde.

So you wish us to revoke the Act of Settlement? Asked the king.

Well, perhaps, if that is what it takes, replied Zedde.

The king thought for a few moments, tapping his cane on the ground lightly, before replying, I will see what we can do, my biggest question is, is Rosenmarkke ready for this?

We are working to muster support, replied Zedde.

Alright then, do so, and well go on from there, thank you gentlemen, replied the king as he rose, the group of men rose and politely tapped their canes on the ground in polite applause, before bowing and then leaving the room.

Are you going to do it? Asked Eleonore as the king and her returned to their coffee.

No, not unless Rosenmarkke shows some interest, a union would severely affect our neutrality, given Rosenmarkkes connections to the wider world, replied the king as they sat down once more.

[b]June 9, 2028: Peace in our Time[/b]
So Wuloosya and Rosenmarkke have ended their little feud, stated Cahit as he rolled into the office of the shah.
Apparently so, I plan on issuing a statement later, replied the shah.
And well get the oil flowing yes? said cahti, patting his belly.
Absolutely, any word on PETROX? asked the Shah.
Cahit frowned, No, no word, they vote terribly slow, 
The shah chuckled, I see why we stay out of these sort of things,
Yes, but it is a necessity, replied Cahit.
Very true, replied the Shah, Anything to lower the debt,
Cahit frowned, I was considering, the bailout offer, 
You were? asked the shah in mild shock.
Yes, I think we should accept it, replied Cahit, Itll help the markets, 
Were you not nearly turning red? joked the shah.
Yes, but it turned out my blood pressure medication hadnt been taken that day, or at all to be frank, replied Cahit, I feel better now, 
Thats good to hear, how are the anger management classes? asked the shah.
They are invigorating, the lady speaks slower than a snail, replied Cahit with a chortle.
Well then, it seems we have some peace in our time, do you have some tapenade? asked the shah, sitting behind his desk.
Of course! chortled Cahit, wiggling his fat fingers and pulling out a jar and crackers from his bag, Did you bring the coffee? asked Cahit.
Yes, replied the shah as the doors opened and the coffee brewer was brought and set on the desk with some dainty cups.
Well then, to peace, to prosperity, chortled Cahit.
To peace and prosperity, replied the shah.

May 24, 2028

From the coastal district of Lavs Anlynd City, South Beach Bay became the center of celebration as it hosted a historic festival the first-ever LGBTQ Multicultural Species Festival. Organized by the city government, the event marked the anniversary of the Rukatis communitys liberation from decades of segregation and systemic discrimination.

The festival was a large scale music concerts, cultural conventions, nightclub gatherings, and a wide array of LGBTQ+ events. Over 450,000 attendees, both foreign visitors and citizens of Oceanica, flooded South Beach to take part in the event.

Festivities officially began at 5:40 PM, continuing deep into the night.  By midnight, the celebration had reached its peak.

At 12:08 AM, everything changed. Five individuals, later identified as members of a far-right neo-human extremist group, initiated a coordinated attack. Armed and deliberate, they opened fire into densely packed areas of the festival. Panic spread instantly as the sounds of gunfire shattered the night. What had been progress events turned into one of the deadliest mass shootings in the history of the United States of Oceanica.

The first gunshots sent waves of confusion through South Beach Bay. For several seconds, many attendees mistook the noise for fireworks until the screams began. Within moments, panic erupted.

Thousands surged in every direction, stampeding through festival grounds, overturning barriers, and abandoning belongings in a desperate attempt to escape. Emergency lines were flooded with calls as witnesses reported multiple shooters. 

By 12:11 AM, the Lavs Anlynd City Police Department had received dozens of confirmed reports of an active mass shooting. Officers stationed nearby were the first to respond, rushing toward the sound of gunfire while directing civilians away from danger. Within minutes, additional units, including tactical response teams, were dispatched.

At 12:16 AM, law enforcement engaged the attackers. The confrontation was brief but intense. Three of the assailants were neutralized at the scene, while two attempted to flee toward the marina district before being apprehended after a short pursuit. Authorities later confirmed that all five suspects were part of an organized extremist group, driven by neo-human supremacist ideology targeting non-human and LGBTQ communities.

Emergency medical services arrived almost immediately after police secured the area. Ambulances, fire rescue teams, and volunteer medics were fast responding at South Beach. Makeshift triage zones were established along the promenade, where the injured were treated under overwhelming conditions.

Local hospitals entered mass casualty protocols. Doctors and nurses worked through the night as victims were transported in waves. Blood banks issued urgent calls for donations, and neighboring cities dispatched additional medical personnel to assist. Families gathered outside emergency rooms, desperately seeking news of loved ones.

By sunrise, the scale of the tragedy became clear. Dozens were confirmed dead, with hundreds more injured, many critically. The South Beach Shooting quickly became one of the deadliest attacks in Oceanican history, sending shockwaves across the nation and the international community.

[b]Government and National Response.[/b]

 By early morning, the President of the United States of Oceanica addressed the nation in an emergency broadcast. Condemning the attack as an act of terror against unity, identity, and freedom, the President declared a national day of mourning and ordered flags to be flown at half staff.

Federal agencies from the Federal Bureau of Special Investigation, took immediate control of the investigation alongside local authorities. Intelligence divisions began tracing the origins of the extremist group, uncovering online networks, funding channels, and potential affiliates.
Security was heightened nationwide.

Major cities increased police presence at public gatherings, particularly at LGBTQ+ venues and multicultural centers. Borders and transport hubs were placed on elevated alert as officials assessed the possibility of further coordinated attacks.

[b]Public Reaction[/b]

Within hours, vigils began forming across Lavs Anlynd City candles lining sidewalks, flowers covering barricades, and messages of love and defiance written in chalk along the streets of South Beach. Social media was flooded with tributes, as the names and faces of victims began to emerge.

Governor of Lavs Anlynd the First Lady and Rukits Sheep, Merry Hill issued statements of support, condemning extremism and expressing condolences. Advocacy groups called for stronger protections against hate driven violence, while communities mourn the lost.

[b]The Announcement[/b]

Taking a sip of water from his metal bottle, Walter Palm stands just behind the press stage within the Joint Counterterror Center. Last time he stood here it was to announce one of his greatest successes as director, now he must talk about one of the biggest attacks in almost 20 years. 

An assistant walks from just off stage and puts his hand on Palms shoulder. Its time, director. Everything is ready.

After sighing, Palm takes the stage. The room is filled with news crews, diplomats, and families of the victims all focused on the podium.

Yesterday, May 24th, 2028, we experienced the largest terrorist attack in USO history. Extremists killed 68 people and injured nearly 220 more, among these 43 lavian citizens injured or killed. This attack was perpetrated by a hate group, a group we work with the FBSI to find and persecute to the fullest extent of the law. We will not rest till these murders are brought to justice, either that be behind bars or in the ground.

[quote=british_calradia;61594641]The economy of the NBE is a very diverse in terms of what it's makeup is and what it produces. Primary, secondary and tertiary sectors are abundant and common within the Empire with each province having vastly different makeups unique to it's geographic position and political history. Private property is effectively guaranteed although all land is technically "leased" out by the Emperor himself. Foreign companies are permitted to operate within the Empire, albeit that they accept the dominance of Balionic companies in terms of logistics (IE, transport companies) and have a local subsidiary headquartered within the Empire or else foreign companies face higher tariffs and legal prohibitions. Tariffs exist as a baseline for all foreign companies but are reduced depending on how rare their product/service is within the Empire and/or if a local subsidiary is set up. 

Foreign investment is very much welcomed, especially in the booming cities of the Empire, where skyscrapers are rapidly being built and the frontier regions of the Empire which seek settlers and investment. Assets can be seized if deemed that the foreign nation is a threat (IE, at war like is the case with Gaesun) and/or dominate over local companies, individuals and aristocratic claims. But such seizures are rare considering the legal benefits natives have and that in the cases that certain areas need investment, they will likely have to be dealt in a court. [/quote]

[b]The Chancellor Speaks[/b]

The dock authorities, though confused at these strange men, bring them to the seat of the Chancellor, who greets them diligently. He offers warm beverages and sweets as they sit in his meeting place, a surprisingly comfortable, almost living room within his larger offices. Books litter the shelves, spelling out words in Shamatine along their spines. The Chancellor, an Imam and well learned man, has a great beard of grey. He is well-aged, though his mind remains sharp. He listens to the briefing laid forth by the junior diplomats before turning to whom he assumes to be the most senior.

[i]"Why would the Sealiph wish to enter into diplomatic relations with someone who sunk a vessel northbound, and one with, may the Divine forgive me for saying, pleasure ships?"[/i] The inquiry was simple but cutting.

[i]"That would be who you seek."[/i] Said the Iroccoan crew member, well-versed in Dwarven things. The bird, who once took a swipe at them now seemed to calm realising what it was truly faced with, the rider at its back, Thaynguard Cartorous lands upon the deck of the outdated ship, greeting the Iroccoan stoutly with a firm handshake, [i]"Good to see you brother, its been too long, and who are these milk drinkers sailing along the Dirja in such an outdated vessel, did nobody tell them about the train?"[/i] The Iroccoan gave a hearty laugh and turned to Dr E. "Indy" Jones, [i]"This is who your Thane spoke to."[/i]

Thaynguard Cartorous extended his hand to Indy.

[b]OOC:[/b] He is like 4 foot 2 in full plate armour, including a beard guard, though he removed that when greeting the Iroccoan.[/quote]
[b][u]The Delegation replies[/u][/b]
The lead delegate from the NBE has changed to a tall, bearded and well dressed man named as "Lord H" who replies to the Chancellor in a candid way;

"Chancellor, you must realise that the sinking of the HMS Godiva is not reflective upon our Empire. The man responsible, Mr Glenn Quagmire is locked up in some prison on a floating prison ship south of Argos. You and your people have nothing to worry about. Afterall, our remaining "pleasure ships" have been sanitised and converted into luxury 'exploration' ships meaning that they are essentially a combination of a floating museum, international hotel and a carnival if that makes sense and we hope that at some point, your nation may accept and partake in this new kind of ship."

The rest of the Balionic delegation nod along with Lord H then saying; "Now. Let's get back to topic. What do you think of our plans? We understand that your nation requires many things that our Empire can help supply"

[b][u]The Expedition[/u][/b]

Dr Indy Jones then returns the handshake, albeit by bending down.

"It is a pleasure meeting you Cartorous, though I wish we were not called milk drinkers as told by our translator we hired and that we should have took the train instead of this crapheap of a ship" he states slightly frustrated.

He then goes on to say, "We were told about your peoples all the way from the other end of Erene and we wish to further know and study your peoples much more indepthy, possibly the most indepth it's ever been. We want to know everything, so that greater recognition from the wider world can be brought to your peoples" 

Calls are then made to the bridge of the steamer to dock at the nearest harbour and the plan is to follow the Thaynguard towards his homeland and peoples. Before that happens, the expedition team manages to already document the local wildlife and environment they have so far seen along the river Dirja, along with demographic studies of the normal Iroccon people.
